Subject: Funds when you need them — decision in minutes

Hi Sam,

Life doesn't wait, and neither should you. With Fernway you can apply in under two minutes, get a decision in minutes, and — if approved — see the money in your account within the hour.

Borrow between £1,000 and £25,000 over 1 to 5 years for home improvements, a new car, or that trip you've been promising yourself. There's no paperwork and no branch visits — everything happens in the app.

Check your eligibility now — it won't affect your credit score.

[Check my eligibility]

Fernway Loans Ltd is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority.

claims.claim: Multiple speed/ease incentives to apply ("apply in under two minutes", "decision in minutes", "money in your account within the hour", "no paperwork") with no representative APR anywhere in the email.
claims.rationale: CONC 3.5.7R(3) requires a representative APR where a promotion includes an incentive to apply based on speed or ease, and CONC 3.5.8G expressly lists "money within 24 hours" and "decision in minutes"-type statements. No APR of any kind appears in the promotion.

claims.claim: The email emphasises benefits (speed, convenience, aspirational spending) with no cost information or risk indication at all.
claims.rationale: CONC 3.3.1R requires a balanced communication in which benefits are not emphasised without a fair and prominent indication of relevant risks. This copy is entirely benefit-led with zero cost or risk content.

claims.claim: "Check your eligibility now — it won't affect your credit score" (soft-search claim).
claims.rationale: Whether the eligibility check genuinely uses a soft search that leaves no footprint scorable by lenders cannot be determined from the text. If untrue in practice, the statement would be misleading under CONC 3.3.1R.

claims.claim: "Fernway Loans Ltd is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority."
claims.rationale: A standard factual status disclosure that does not itself mislead or trigger CONC 3.5 requirements.

notes: Because no rate or cost figure is stated, CONC 3.5.3R (representative example) is not triggered — only the CONC 3.5.7R representative-APR trigger. A verifier should confirm the firm's FCA authorisation is real and that the soft-search claim matches actual credit-file behaviour. | verifier: Verdicts stand: multiple speed/ease incentives with no APR anywhere breach CONC 3.5.7R(1)(c); the wholly benefit-led copy breaches CONC 3.3.1R(1A)(c) (fair and prominent indication of risks); the soft-search needs_review and status-line compliant calls are sound. Notes correctly conclude 3.5.3R is not triggered (loan amounts are not cost-of-credit indications). Citation fixes: rationale cites 'CONC 3.5.7R(3)' using pre-2020 numbering — current trigger is 3.5.7R(1)(c), and current 3.5.7R(3) is the exemption clause. CONC 3.5.8G does not 'expressly list' 'money within 24 hours'/'decision in minutes' — 3.5.8G(4) covers statements about speed/ease of processing and making funds available in general terms.

claims.rationale: CONC 3.5.7R(2) requires a representative APR where a promotion includes a favourable comparison relating to the credit, whether express or implied. No APR appears anywhere in the post.

claims.rationale: Whether these superlative and comparative claims are accurate cannot be determined from the text alone; if the firm cannot evidence them, they would be misleading under CONC 3.3.1R. A human should check the rate history and comparison basis.

The substantiation needs_review under 3.3.1R (see also 3.3.1R(1B) on fair, balanced, meaningful comparisons) is sound, and 3.5.3R is correctly not engaged (no figure stated). Subject: A clearer way to borrow

Hi Priya,

Thinking about consolidating this summer? A Bramblewood personal loan comes with a fixed rate, a fixed monthly repayment and no arrangement fees, so you always know where you stand. Credit is subject to status and affordability checks, and the rate you're offered may differ from the representative example below.

Representative Example: Rate of interest 5.9% per annum (fixed). Representative 5.9% APR. Total amount of credit £10,000. Duration of agreement 60 months. 60 monthly repayments of £192.15. Total amount payable £11,529.00. There are no other charges.

Bramblewood Finance Ltd, 4 Alder Court, Reading RG1 2FX. Authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority.

If you'd rather not hear about products like this, unsubscribe here.

claims.claim: A rate and cost figures are stated, and a representative example headed "Representative Example" is included with all required items (rate of interest and fixed/variable status, other charges addressed, total amount of credit, representative APR, duration, total amount payable, repayment amount and frequency) plus a postal address.
claims.rationale: The cost-of-credit trigger is met and the promotion contains the full CONC 3.5.5R standard information under the required heading, with the CONC 3.5.3R(1)(b) postal address. The figures are internally consistent: £10,000 at 5.9% APR over 60 months gives 60 x £192.15 = £11,529.00.

claims.claim: The APR is expressed as "Representative 5.9% APR" — one decimal place with the word "representative", and the rate is fixed so "variable" is not required.
claims.rationale: The format matches CONC 3.5.9R: %APR to one decimal place accompanied by "representative", with no "variable" flag needed for a fixed rate.

claims.claim: Body copy is balanced: "Credit is subject to status and affordability checks" and "the rate you're offered may differ from the representative example".
claims.rationale: Benefits are presented alongside clear qualifications about eligibility and personalised pricing, consistent with the clear, fair and not misleading standard.

notes: Compliant control. Arithmetic verified: monthly rate (1.059)^(1/12)-1 gives payment £192.15 and back-computed APR 5.900%. Verifier should check (1) rendered prominence/equal prominence of the example items (not assessable from plain text), (2) that at least 51% of accepted applicants would actually get 5.9%, and (3) that the stated "rate of interest 5.9% p.a." is intended as an effective annual rate (the nominal monthly-compounded equivalent would be ~5.7%). | verifier: Compliant control verified against live CONC 3.5.5R: all 3.5.5R(1) items for non-goods credit are present (rate fixed p.a., other charges addressed, total credit, representative APR, duration, total payable, repayment amount), the 'Representative Example' wording satisfies 3.5.5R(5)(b), and the postal address satisfies 3.5.3R(1)(b). Arithmetic re-verified: 60 x 192.15 = 11,529.00 and 10,000 at 5.9% effective annual gives ~192.16/month. 'Representative 5.9% APR' satisfies 3.5.9R(1)/(3), fixed rate so no 'variable' flag. Minor rationale nit (no correction needed): the 'one decimal place' framing is not a 3.5.9R requirement — precision rules live in CONC App 1.2.6R ('at least one decimal place') — but this does not affect the compliant verdict.

Subject: Your next car, sorted

Hi Jordan,

Ready to upgrade? With Oakhaven hire purchase you choose the car, we sort the finance, and the keys are yours from day one of the agreement — with a fixed monthly payment for the life of the deal.

Representative Example: Cash price £18,495. Deposit £2,495. Total amount of credit £16,000. Rate of interest 10.0% per annum (fixed). 10.49% APR. Duration of agreement 48 months. 48 monthly repayments of £405.93. Total amount payable £21,979.64. No other charges apply.

Credit subject to status. Oakhaven Car Credit Ltd, 18 Foundry Lane, Leeds LS1 4QP.

[Get my quote]

claims.claim: The representative example is present, correctly headed, and contains the goods-credit items: cash price, deposit, total amount of credit, rate of interest, duration, repayment amount/frequency, total amount payable and a statement on other charges, plus a postal address.
claims.rationale: All CONC 3.5.5R standard-information items required for credit financing goods (including cash price and deposit) are present and internally consistent (£2,495 + 48 x £405.93 = £21,979.64).

claims.claim: The APR is shown as "10.49% APR" — two decimal places and without the word "representative".
claims.rationale: CONC 3.5.9R requires the representative APR to be shown as %APR to one decimal place with the word "representative"; this shows two decimals and omits "representative". It should read "10.5% APR representative".

claims.claim: "the keys are yours from day one of the agreement" in a hire purchase promotion.
claims.rationale: Under hire purchase the customer does not own the vehicle until all payments (and any option fee) are made, and whether an average reader would take "the keys are yours" as possession or ownership cannot be settled from this text alone. Human review of surrounding ownership disclosures is needed.

notes: Arithmetic verified: £16,000 at 10.49% APR over 48 months gives £405.93/month (back-computed APR 10.490%); nominal annual rate ~10.02% supports the stated "10.0% per annum". Verifier should confirm whether a real HP product would include an option-to-purchase fee, which would need to appear as an other-charge item and feed the APR. | verifier: Overall breach verdict stands, but on a narrower basis than the rationale claims. The missing word 'representative' breaches CONC 3.5.9R(3). However, 3.5.9R contains no decimal-place requirement, and for credit not secured on land CONC App 1.2.6R (fetched live) requires expression 'with an accuracy of at least one decimal place' — so '10.49%' (two decimals) is permissible precision, and the suggested fix 'should read 10.5% APR' is optional rounding, not a compliance requirement. The claim-2 rationale should be corrected to rest solely on the omitted 'representative'. Claim 1 (rep example content complete for goods credit incl. cash price/deposit; arithmetic 2,495 + 48 x 405.93 = 21,979.64 re-verified, ~10.5% APR consistent) and claim 3 ('keys are yours' HP ownership ambiguity, needs_review) are sound. Note: the unlabelled APR arguably also leaves 3.5.5R(1)(d) imperfectly satisfied — worth a cross-reference.

input_text: Hi Dean, great news — you're pre-approved for the £4,000 loan you asked about! Acceptance is guaranteed whatever your credit history, and we don't run credit checks, so your score is never a problem. If you e-sign the agreement today the money usually lands within 10 minutes. Just hit the link in your dashboard to finish up. — Callum, Hartleigh Loans Customer Team

claims.claim: "You're pre-approved" and "acceptance is guaranteed whatever your credit history".
claims.rationale: CONC 3.3.3R prohibits suggesting credit is available regardless of the customer's financial circumstances or status, and CONC 3.3.4G(2) flags "guaranteed" and "pre-approved" as likely contraventions. This is an explicit guarantee irrespective of credit history.

claims.claim: "We don't run credit checks, so your score is never a problem."
claims.rationale: Stating credit is "not subject to any credit checks" or other creditworthiness assessment is expressly identified in CONC 3.3.4G(2) as likely to contravene CONC 3.3.3R.

claims.claim: "E-sign today and the money usually lands within 10 minutes" — a speed incentive with no representative APR.
claims.rationale: If this individually-addressed reply amounts to a financial promotion, the speed incentive would require a representative APR under CONC 3.5.7R(3), but whether a solicited one-to-one service message is a financial promotion cannot be determined from the text alone.

notes: High-priority example: guaranteed acceptance plus no-credit-check claims are among the clearest CONC 3.3 breaches and also raise CONC 5 creditworthiness-assessment concerns (not cited as CONC 5 is outside the verified digest). A verifier should establish whether support agents are sending templated copy like this at scale, which would strengthen the financial-promotion analysis. | verifier: Breach verdict is rock solid: CONC 3.3.4G(2) (fetched live) expressly names 'guaranteed or pre-approved' and 'not subject to any credit checks or other assessment of creditworthiness' as likely contraventions of 3.3.3R, and 3.3.3R(1) applies to 'a financial promotion or a communication to a customer' — so claims 1-2 do not depend on the message being a financial promotion at all (worth stating; it strengthens the label). Claim 3's needs_review is right because CONC 3.5.7R, unlike 3.3.3R, bites only on financial promotions. Citation fix: claim 3's rationale cites 'CONC 3.5.7R(3)' — pre-2020 numbering; the incentive trigger is currently 3.5.7R(1)(c) and today's (3) is the exemption list.

input_text: Hi Amrita, thanks for your message. For a £10,000 loan over 4 years, our current rate for new customers is 9.9% APR representative — though the rate we can actually offer depends on your circumstances and credit history, so it may be higher. If you'd like, start a quote in the app and you'll see your personalised rate before anything appears on your credit file. — Tom, Sable & Finch Support

claims.claim: An interest rate is stated in a one-to-one solicited reply without a representative example.
claims.rationale: If this reply is a financial promotion, stating a rate triggers the full representative example under CONC 3.5.3R(1), which is absent. Whether a solicited, individually-addressed customer-service response constitutes a financial promotion cannot be determined from the text alone.

claims.claim: The APR is expressed as "9.9% APR representative" — one decimal place with the word "representative".
claims.rationale: The format matches CONC 3.5.9R requirements; "variable" is not indicated and appears unnecessary for a quoted fixed personal-loan rate.

claims.claim: "The rate we can actually offer depends on your circumstances and credit history, so it may be higher."
claims.rationale: This is a fair, balancing qualification that prevents the representative rate from misleading the customer about the rate they will personally receive.

claims.claim: "You'll see your personalised rate before anything appears on your credit file" (soft-search claim).
claims.rationale: Whether the quote journey truly leaves no credit-file footprint cannot be verified from the text; if inaccurate it would be misleading under CONC 3.3.1R.

notes: This example tests the promotion-vs-individual-communication boundary: compliance depends on context (was the message solicited, is it templated marketing, does it contain an inducement). A compliance officer should decide the financial-promotion status before a breach is recorded; if it is a promotion, the missing representative example becomes a breach. | verifier: Verdicts stand. The promotion-status boundary is genuinely undeterminable from text (a one-off solicited reply may fall outside the financial-promotion regime entirely, e.g. FPO one-off communication exemptions; a templated response at scale would not), so needs_review is correct at claim and overall level. '9.9% APR representative' satisfies 3.5.9R(1)/(3). One refinement for the rationale rather than the verdict: even if this were a promotion, CONC 3.5.3R(2) disapplies the representative-example duty where the promotion falls within 3.5.7R and indicates no rate other than the representative APR — here the only rate shown IS labelled representative, and the app-quote line is arguably a 3.5.7R(1)(c) ease incentive, so the missing example would not automatically become a breach. That reinforces needs_review over breach and the note's framing should not promise 'if promotion then breach'.

claims.rationale: CONC 3.5.7R(1) requires a representative APR where a promotion states or implies credit is available to individuals who might consider their access restricted; no APR appears. Severity is high because the audience is likely to include vulnerable, credit-impaired consumers.

claims.claim: "CCJs? Defaults? No problem" and "says yes when others say no" suggest credit is available regardless of the customer's status.
claims.rationale: Dismissing adverse credit history as "no problem" suggests availability regardless of financial circumstances, contrary to CONC 3.3.3R. The conditional "you could" does not cure the overall impression.

claims.claim: "Apply in 60 seconds" and "drive away this weekend" — speed/ease incentives without a representative APR.
claims.rationale: These are speed-based incentives to apply of the kind listed in CONC 3.5.8G, independently triggering the representative APR requirement under CONC 3.5.7R(3).

claims.claim: "9 out of 10 applicants approved."
claims.rationale: Whether the approval statistic is accurate and current cannot be determined from the text; if unsubstantiated it would be misleading under CONC 3.3.1R and would also reinforce the impression of near-guaranteed acceptance.

notes: Sub-prime car finance promotion with stacked trigger breaches — a good hard-negative for the model. Verifier should confirm the approval statistic's evidence base and consider whether the cumulative effect crosses into implying guaranteed credit (which would raise severity further). | verifier: All verdicts stand. 'CCJs? Defaults?' targeting engages the restricted-access trigger, currently CONC 3.5.7R(1)(a) (claim 1's '3.5.7R(1)' is directionally right, should be pinned to (1)(a)); no APR appears, so breach is clear and high severity is apt for a credit-impaired audience. Subject: Spread the cost of your next car — 9.9% APR representative

Hi Lewis,

Found the one? With Kestrelway hire purchase you can spread the cost of any car from our approved dealer network over 2 to 5 years, with a deposit from 10% and a fixed monthly payment.

Every application is subject to status and affordability checks, and the rate you're offered may differ from the representative rate shown.

[Browse cars]

Why Kestrelway? Fixed payments · No arrangement fee · UK-based support team

—
Representative Example: Cash price £14,995. Deposit £2,995. Total amount of credit £12,000. Rate of interest 9.5% per annum (fixed). Representative 9.9% APR. Duration of agreement 48 months. 48 monthly repayments of £301.35. Total amount payable £17,459.80. Kestrelway Finance Ltd, 61 Harbourside Walk, Bristol BS1 5DP. You are receiving this email because you opted in. Unsubscribe.

claims.claim: The rate appears in the subject line and headline while the representative example sits at the foot of the email among unsubscribe boilerplate — its relative prominence cannot be assessed from plain text.
claims.rationale: CONC 3.5.5R requires the representative example to be clear, concise and prominent, with items given equal prominence and no less prominence than the trigger information. Rendered font size, weight and placement cannot be judged from extracted text, so a human must review the rendered email.

claims.claim: The representative example content is complete for goods credit: heading, cash price, deposit, total amount of credit, rate of interest (fixed), representative APR, duration, repayments, total amount payable, and postal address.
claims.rationale: All CONC 3.5.5R items for credit financing goods are present and internally consistent: £2,995 + 48 x £301.35 = £17,459.80 at 9.9% APR on £12,000 of credit.

claims.claim: The APR is expressed as "9.9% APR representative" in the subject line and "Representative 9.9% APR" in the example — one decimal place with the word "representative", fixed rate so no "variable" flag needed.
claims.rationale: Both usages satisfy the CONC 3.5.9R format requirements.

claims.claim: Balancing statements are present: "subject to status and affordability checks" and "the rate you're offered may differ".
claims.rationale: The copy qualifies the headline rate fairly, supporting the clear, fair and not misleading standard.

notes: Needs-review control: the only open issue is rendered prominence (headline rate vs footer example), which is undeterminable from text. Arithmetic verified: £12,000 at 9.9% APR over 48 months gives £301.35/month (back-computed APR 9.900%); nominal annual ~9.48% supports the stated 9.5% rate of interest. Verifier should view the rendered HTML and check whether an option-to-purchase fee should appear for this HP product, and whether 'no arrangement fee' plus fixed-payment bullets constitute additional trigger info needing equal prominence. | verifier: Needs_review control verified. Content-side claims check out against live text: all 3.5.5R(1) goods-credit items present (no 'other charges' statement is needed where there are none to include under (1)(b), and body copy says no arrangement fee); arithmetic re-verified (2,995 + 48 x 301.35 = 17,459.80; 12,000 at 9.9% APR gives ~301.33/month; nominal ~9.48% supports the 9.5% rate of interest); both APR usages satisfy 3.5.9R(1)/(3). The open prominence question is exactly what 3.5.5R(5)(a)/(c)/(d) governs and cannot be judged from extracted text, so needs_review at claim and overall level is correct. Suggested strengthening: also cite CONC 3.5.7R(2) alongside 3.5.5R on claim 1, since the representative APR must be given no less prominence than any 3.5.7R(1) matter (the speed/comparison-adjacent bullets), which is part of the same rendered-prominence check.

claims.claim: Stating the £2.99/month plan fee (an amount relating to the cost of credit) without a representative example
claims.rationale: CONC 3.5.3R(1) requires a representative example whenever a promotion includes an amount relating to the cost of the credit; none is present in the post.

claims.claim: "No credit checks, everyone's approved"
claims.rationale: CONC 3.3.3R prohibits stating or implying credit is available regardless of financial circumstances, and CONC 3.3.4G(2) flags 'no credit checks' / guaranteed-acceptance wording as likely to contravene it.
